co.n: The Liturgical Year & Sacred Seasons Cohort

c.p: What is the summit and highest point of the entire Catholic Liturgical Year?
c.a: the sacred paschal triduum and easter sunday | easter and the sacred paschal triduum | the paschal triduum | easter sunday | easter
c.h: The three great days spanning Holy Thursday, Good Friday, Holy Saturday, and Easter Sunday.
c.e: The Sacred Paschal Triduum—celebrating Christ's Last Supper, Passion, Death, Burial, and glorious Resurrection on Easter—is the summit of the whole liturgical year (CCC 1168-1169).
r: the opening of the school year in september
The civil or academic calendar is separate; the summit of the Church's liturgical year is Easter and the Sacred Paschal Triduum.

c.p: How long does the joyful Easter Season (Eastertide) last in the Catholic Church, and on which solemn feast does it conclude?
c.a: 50 days concluding on pentecost sunday | fifty days ending on pentecost | 50 days pentecost | 50 days concluding with pentecost
c.h: Counted from Easter Sunday to the descent of the Holy Spirit on Our Lady and the Apostles.
c.e: The Easter season lasts 50 glorious days, celebrated as 'one great Sunday', concluding with Pentecost Sunday, the birthday of the Church (CCC 731, 1169).
r: Easter is not just a single weekend; the Easter season continues for fifty full days until Pentecost Sunday.

c.p: What are the four main liturgical colours worn by the priest, and what does the colour green signify during Ordinary Time?
c.a: green white purple and red, with green symbolizing life, hope, and spiritual growth | green signifies life hope and spiritual growth | hope and spiritual growth | green white purple red
c.h: Think of green plants and trees flourishing as we walk with Jesus in daily discipleship.
c.e: The principal liturgical colours are Green (Ordinary Time - hope and spiritual growth), Purple (Advent/Lent - penance), White/Gold (Easter/Christmas - joy and resurrection), and Red (Pentecost/Martyrs - fire of the Holy Spirit) (CCC 1155).
r: green is used because it is the priest's favourite colour
Liturgical colours are sacred symbols established by the universal Church, not personal preferences.
